Tropical Weather Outlook

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Dolly, located over the central tropical Atlantic.

Tropical cyclone formation is not expected during the next 7 days.

item.title: Tropical Storm Dolly Public Advisory Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM AST Thu Aug 27 2026 
000
WTNT34 KNHC 280244
TCPAT4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Dolly Advisory Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL042026
1100 PM AST Thu Aug 27 2026
 
...DOLLY CONTINUES MOVING RAPIDLY WESTWARD...
...INTERESTS IN THE LEEWARD ISLANDS SHOULD MONITOR ITS PROGRESS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 1100 PM AST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
-----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...13.8N 42.3W
ABOUT 1315 MI...2120 KM E OF THE LEEWARD ISLANDS
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 280 DEGREES AT 23 MPH...37 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1007 MB...29.74 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
Interests in the Leeward Islands should monitor the progress of
Dolly.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 PM AST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Dolly was
located near latitude 13.8 North, longitude 42.3 West.  Dolly is
moving toward the west near 23 mph (37 km/h), and this motion is
expected to continue for the next couple of days.  On the forecast
track, this system should be nearing the Leeward Islands this
weekend.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is likely during the next 48 hours, and 
Dolly is forecast to degenerate into a tropical wave before it 
reaches the Leeward Islands.

Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles (185 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1007 mb (29.74 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Dolly can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDAT4 and WMO header WTNT44 KNHC.

RAINFALL: Heavy rain from Dolly could affect the Leeward Islands 
late Saturday into Sunday, with rainfall moving into the Virgin 
Islands, Puerto Rico and Hispaniola Sunday and Monday.  This heavy 
rain may produce flash flooding within areas of higher terrain of 
the Leeward Islands.
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 500 AM AST.
 
$$
Forecaster Pasch

item.title: Tropical Storm Dolly Forecast Discussion Number 3
item.description:
Issued at 1100 PM AST Thu Aug 27 2026 
000
WTNT44 KNHC 280244
TCDAT4
 
Tropical Storm Dolly Discussion Number   3
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL042026
1100 PM AST Thu Aug 27 2026

Dolly appears to be more or less maintaining its intensity at this 
time.  However, the associated deep convection is not very 
well-organized, with no well-defined banding features evident on 
satellite images.  The center of circulation is estimated to be on 
the north side of the main area of convection.  The Dvorak 
intensity estimate from TAFB remains at 35 kt.  There was a 
Metop-B scatterometer pass from just before 00Z which showed just a
couple of 35-kt vectors.  Therefore the advisory intensity is kept 
at 35 kt.  The scatterometer pass did not completely capture the 
circulation of the storm but it did suggest some 
north-northeastward to south-southwestward elongation of the center.

The storm continues to move quickly toward the west and the initial 
motion estimate is 280/20 kt, about the same as before.  Dolly is 
forecast to move mainly westward at a fast forward speed for the 
next couple of days on the south side of a strong high pressure 
ridge over the central Atlantic.  There have been no significant 
changes in the track guidance from earlier today.  There is 
fairly good agreement amongst the various model tracks, and the 
official track forecast is roughly in the middle of these tracks.  
This is close to the latest Google DeepMind solution.

Although it will encounter warmer ocean waters, Dolly is likely to 
move into less favorable atmospheric conditions during the next 
couple of days.  Some slight short-term strengthening is possible, 
but increasing vertical wind shear, relatively dry air and the 
fast forward motion of the system should begin to adversely affect 
Dolly fairly soon.  The global models show the system degenerating 
into a tropical wave while it approaches the Lesser Antilles, and 
the NHC intensity forecast is close to the model consensus.   
Post-tropical positions are provided at 48-60h given the risk of 
gusty winds and heavy rainfall.
 
KEY MESSAGES:
 
1. Heavy rains from Dolly or its remnants could affect the Leeward
Islands late Saturday into Sunday with possible impacts in the
Virgin Islands, Puerto Rico, and Hispaniola Sunday and Monday.  This
heavy rain may produce flash flooding, especially in areas of
higher terrain of the Leeward Islands.
